correctness.rationale: For the 10-vertex Petersen graph with fifteen unit-rate edge clocks, successful attempts are an embedded random-edge matching process with conditional edge probability 1/r and independent Exp(r) holding times. Backward absorption gives the terminal law (3:1/25, 4:52/75, 5:4/15); complete histories give 71 labelled terminal matchings (five size-3, sixty size-4, six size-5). In a separately written Kneser(5,2) path enumeration, all 2,190 complete success histories and exact rational hypoexponential residues reproduced the advertised mean EX(t)=317/75-(4/7)e^-t-(25/26)e^-2t-(10/7)e^-3t-(7/25)e^-5t-(7/9)e^-6t-(67/350)e^-10t-(326/20475)e^-15t. Coefficient sum zero at t=0 and derivative 15; limiting mean 317/75. Each path has strictly descending positive rates, so no repeated-rate pole. The finite computation is exhaustive for this specified finite graph, and the exact CTMC/hypoexponential derivation covers all t>=0, not other graphs.
